review.reason: The frozen acceptance file is self-contained, uses real loaders/transforms, the real ReportingService over real DuckDBStore/PostgresReportingStore, the real FastAPI router via TestClient, and real OIDC permission-bound auth (MockOidcIssuer + AppSettings.from_env + build_oidc_provider/build_session_manager). Every import and constructor signature referenced resolves on the canonical base (verified: build_oidc_provider/build_session_manager shim, MockOidcIssuer, running_postgres_container, RunMetadataRepository, IngestionConfigRepository, AccountTransactionService, subscription_charge_id, load_subscriptions/load_contract_prices/load_transactions). The source_key()/item_id encodings exactly match the item_id strings built in transformation_overview.py (anomaly_/review_/renewal_/upcoming_ prefixes and underscore/slash separators), and the four source segments, row-model names, and the attention-items segment match report_routes.py/response_models.py. The remaining 'tautology' blocking property is closed: _observe_source_queries replays each source-relation query on the RAW DuckDB connection cursor (not the possibly-mocked method) and _assert_observed_selection asserts the full opaque item_id is bound as a parameter (not inlined, not split), a WHERE with %s/? appears before any LIMIT, the identity columns are selected, and every actually-returned row's source_key equals the requested item_id — so 'WHERE %s=%s [item_id,item_id]', fetch-all-then-filter, and returning the first/equal-looking row all fail. The record route is absent on base (9cf62c...), so every test fails with 404/route-missing (missing-record behavior), never a collection/import/fixture error; no test passes vacuously on base. No new grants or auth-policy edits are required because the path-based policy derives reports.read.publication.<first_segment> for the /reports/<segment>/records/{item_id} path, which the auth tests assert. The Postgres case skips cleanly when Docker is absent rather than claiming a pass. Minor, non-blocking gaps: api.d.ts is only checked by string containment (not structural type equality), and no assertion positively forbids landing-table reads (a scope constraint rather than an acceptance property). Neither undermines the outcome assertions.
review.trivial_pass: Attacks attempted and why each fails: (1) Constant/hardcoded rows — HTTP tests compare against expected_records() derived from the real list endpoints and real store facts (CURRENT_DATE-derived d10/d20, deterministic charge ids), so canned rows cannot match; the instrumentation tests additionally require an observed source query, which a hardcoded route never emits (assert source fails). (2) Mocking/replacing the subject — the tests construct TransformationService(DuckDBStore.memory()), ReportingService, and create_app themselves from real classes; there is no injection seam for a mock, and the instrumentation replays SQL on database.connection.cursor() directly, so even a tampered store.fetchall_dicts returning canned rows would still be exposed by the raw replay. (3) Ignored input / returning another record — body['item_id'] == item_id and all(source_key(row) == item_id) plus item_id in params (full opaque key) reject cross-record and split-key answers. (4) Tautology WHERE %s=%s [item_id,item_id] or fetch-all-then-limit — the replay executes the actual SQL against real data, so any query returning the whole relation fails all(source_key(row) == item_id); the 'limit not before where' and 'where with ?/%s' checks block subquery-limit and no-WHERE variants. (5) Underscore/slash splitting — item_id must appear verbatim in params and must not appear in the SQL text. No trivial path passes.
checks: All imports/symbols resolve on base: build_oidc_provider/build_session_manager (shared.auth shim), MockOidcIssuer, running_postgres_container, RunMetadataRepository, IngestionConfigRepository, AccountTransactionService, subscription_charge_id, load_subscriptions/load_contract_prices/load_transactions.
source_key()/item_id encodings match transformation_overview.py item_id construction for all four kinds (anomaly_/review_/renewal_/upcoming_ with underscore and slash separators).

Source segments (transaction-anomalies, contract-review-candidates, contract-renewal-watchlist, upcoming-fixed-costs) and row-model names match report_routes.py and response_models.py; mart columns (reason, renewal_date, charge_id, expected_date, transaction_id) are real.
Seed expectations (240 anomalies, 4 review, 4 renewal, 2 upcoming) and component/equal-looking identities are consistent with the existing transformation logic, so no fixture inventing.

Permission strings (reports.read.publication.attention-items and .<segment>) and the 'X permission required.' 403 detail match permission_registry/middleware_authorization; path-based policy covers the new /reports/<segment>/records/{item_id} route with no new grant.

Instrumentation (_observe_source_queries + _assert_observed_selection) replays the actual SQL on the raw DuckDB cursor and requires full-key parameter binding, WHERE before LIMIT, identity-column selection, and source_key==item_id on real returned rows — closing tautology, fetch-all-then-filter, and mock/canned-row attacks.
Record route absent on base: every test fails with 404/route-missing (missing-record behavior), not collection/import/fixture errors; no test passes vacuously.
Encoded-slash round-trip through the real router is exercised via quote(item_id, safe='') for review/renewal ids containing '/'.
Published-authority boundaries (no warehouse fallback), stale-NULL 503 vs provable-unknown 404, partial-NULL 503, and unpublished-relation 503 are each asserted through real HTTP responses.

No source-data leakage in failures asserted via whole-field forbidden tokens (source names, contract ids, charge ids, dates), not a numeric substring blacklist; failure bodies are {detail}-only while legitimate 422/validation echoes client input.
OpenAPI.json regeneration is enforced (generated path must equal live path with item_id/rows schema); api.d.ts is checked by path containment.
Disposable Postgres case is a separate @slow/@integration target that skips (pytest.skip) when Docker is unavailable, never claiming a skipped case passed.
Time is deterministic: today read from the same authoritative store (SELECT CURRENT_DATE), d10/d20 derived, expectations derived from the same store facts.
